Done. I implemented the model exactly as system_info.json specifies, ran all 30 grid points x 2 replicates (60 stochastic trajectories), and produced all four artifacts in the working directory. Runtime ~68 s.

ARTIFACTS (all present, validated):
- simulate.py (self-contained; no CLI args/placeholders; matplotlib Agg primary path + a pure-Python PNG fallback so it runs even where matplotlib is absent — matplotlib was not installable in my sandbox, so the PNG here is from the fallback; in an env with matplotlib it yields a matplotlib figure).
- ca_traces.npz: 30 keys ip3{i}_N{j}, each float64 (2,1200). Verified all keys/shapes/dtypes.
- summary_stats.json: all 7 keys, null for NaN.
- calcium_summary.png: valid 1180x860 four-panel figure (trace, period vs IP3, CV vs N, p_open vs IP3); decoded and confirmed all 4 panels have axes + data lines.

WHAT THE TIME COURSES LOOK LIKE (confirms our earlier finding):
- Every trace shows ONE large initial transient spike (Ca_cyt 0.1 -> ~1.5-1.6 uM within ~1 s) then relaxes to a quasi-steady state (~0.9 uM at mid/high IP3) with only small irregular bumps. No sustained relaxation oscillations.
- p_open (N=800, time-averaged, increasing with IP3): [0.00582, 0.00793, 0.00968, 0.01368, 0.01722, 0.02147].
- conservation_error_max = 5.44e-14 (machine precision; both compartments integrated, drift tracked every sub-step across all 60 runs).

SUMMARY STATISTICS (per your approved option-a rules):
- cr_ip3_idx_used = 1 (idx 1 chosen over idx 0: it yields more detectable ISIs across the five N values).
- period_vs_ip3 (N=800) = [null x 6]. With prominence = 0.3*(max-min), each N=800 replicate has EXACTLY 1 peak (the initial transient, t~0.7-1.2 s) at every IP3 -> <2 peaks -> NaN. This faithfully reflects that the largest channel count does not oscillate; I did not force a period from a single spike.
- cv_isi_vs_N (idx 1) = [0.984, 0.581, 0.114, null, null] for N=[5,20,80,250,800]. Defined where >=2 ISIs exist (N=5:11 ISI, N=20:13, N=80:2); null at N=250,800 (only 1 spike each). Trend: CV falls as N grows (more regular at higher N) until the system settles.

KEY LIMITATION / THING TO FLAG:
- period_vs_ip3 is entirely null. This is the honest outcome of (i) the model genuinely not oscillating at N=800, (ii) your prominence floor of 0.3*(range) finding only the single transient spike, and (iii) the task fixing period_vs_ip3 at the largest N. If you'd like any period values, the only levers within the spec would be a lower prominence (you set a floor of 0.3*range, so I did not drop below it) or a different period definition — I can explore that if you want, but as specified the correct answer is null. Everything else (traces, p_open, CV where defined, conservation) is solid.
